references.text: Paul quotes directly from Deuteronomy 32:35 when he writes 'Vengeance is mine, I will repay, says the Lord', and applies this to Christians' relationship with their enemies.
The author of Hebrews quotes this verse directly: 'We know him who said, Vengeance is mine, I will repay', as a warning against falling away.
The psalm calls upon God as 'the God of vengeance' and asks Him to reveal Himself, reflecting the theme of God's vengeance from Deuteronomy 32:35.
Isaiah speaks of 'a day of vengeance for the Lord', which reflects the same theme of God's coming judgment and retribution.
The Lord declares that 'the day of vengeance was in my heart', linking to God's sovereign right to avenge as expressed in Deuteronomy 32:35.
Jeremiah refers to 'a day of vengeance' where the Lord takes vengeance on His enemies, consistent with the theme in the Song of Moses.
Proverbs teaches 'Do not say, I will repay evil! Wait for the Lord, and He will save you', which is built on the principle that vengeance belongs to God.
The command not to take revenge or hold a grudge is based on the same principle: vengeance belongs to God, not to humans.
